request: do students who study longer score higher?

beats.intent: Axes of hours studied against test score with ten students as dots
beats.narration: Each dot is one student: hours of study across, test score up.
beats.code:
stage.title("Study time and scores")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 10), y_range=(0, 100), labels=("hours", "score"))
pts = plot_points(stage, ax, [(1, 42), (2, 50), (2.5, 47), (3, 58), (4, 61), (5, 66), (6, 70), (7, 79), (8, 83), (9, 88)])
stage.caption("Ten students, one dot each")

beats.intent: The dots on the right half highlighted, all higher than those on the left
beats.narration: The students who studied more than five hours all sit higher up the chart.
beats.code:
right = VGroup(*pts[5:])
highlight(stage, right)
stage.caption("More hours, higher scores")

beats.intent: A dashed arrow rising through the cloud of dots from lower left to upper right
beats.narration: The cloud rises from left to right: the two quantities go up together. That is a positive correlation.
beats.code:
trend = draw_arrow(stage, ax.c2p(0.5, 38), ax.c2p(9.5, 92))
stage.caption("Rising together: a positive correlation")

beats.intent: Axes with dots rising from lower left to upper right
beats.narration: When one quantity grows as the other grows, the dots climb to the right.
beats.code:
stage.title("Positive correlation")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 10), y_range=(0, 10), where="left")
up = plot_points(stage, ax, [(1, 1.5), (2, 2.2), (3, 3.4), (4, 3.9), (5, 5.3), (6, 5.8), (7, 7.1), (8, 7.6), (9, 9.0)])
stage.caption("Both go up together")

beats.intent: Fresh axes with dots falling from upper left to lower right
beats.narration: When one grows while the other shrinks, the dots fall to the right: a negative correlation.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
stage.title("Negative correlation")
ax2 = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 10), y_range=(0, 10))
down = plot_points(stage, ax2, [(1, 9.1), (2, 8.0), (3, 7.4), (4, 6.1), (5, 5.2), (6, 4.6), (7, 3.1), (8, 2.4), (9, 1.2)], color=RED)
stage.caption("One up, the other down")

beats.intent: Fresh axes with dots scattered with no trend at all
beats.narration: And when the dots show no direction at all, there is no correlation.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
stage.title("No correlation")
ax3 = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 10), y_range=(0, 10))
none = plot_points(stage, ax3, [(1, 6), (2, 2), (3, 8), (4, 4), (5, 7), (6, 1.5), (7, 5), (8, 8.5), (9, 3)], color=GREEN)
stage.caption("No direction, no correlation")

request: how does one outlier drag the average?

beats.intent: A number line from 0 to 20 with five data points and the mean marked
beats.narration: Five values: four, five, six, six and nine. Their mean is six.
beats.code:
stage.title("Pulling the average")
nl = draw_number_line(stage, x_range=(0, 20))
for v in (4, 5, 6, 6, 9):
    mark_point(stage, nl, v)
m = mark_point(stage, nl, 6, color=RED)
stage.caption("The mean is 6 (red)")

beats.intent: A sixth point at 20 appears far to the right and the mean marker slides to 8.3
beats.narration: Add one extreme value, twenty. The mean slides right to about eight point three.
beats.code:
out = mark_point(stage, nl, 20, color=ORANGE, label="outlier")
stage.play(m.animate.move_to(nl.n2p(8.33)), run_time=1.5)
stage.caption("One outlier drags the mean to 8.33")

beats.intent: The equation (4+5+6+6+9+20)/6 = 8.33 beside the number line
beats.narration: Every value counts equally in the mean, so one big value pulls hard.

request: how fast does a population of bacteria grow if it doubles every hour?

beats.intent: Axes of hours against bacteria with dots at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32
beats.narration: Start with one bacterium. Every hour each one splits in two: one, two, four, eight, sixteen, thirty two.
beats.code:
stage.title("Doubling every hour")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 6), y_range=(0, 70), labels=("hours", "bacteria"))
pts = plot_points(stage, ax, [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 8), (4, 16), (5, 32)])
stage.caption("1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32")

beats.intent: The curve 2^t drawn through the dots and on to 64 at hour 6
beats.narration: A smooth curve, two to the t, passes through every dot and keeps getting steeper.
beats.code:
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda t: 2 ** t, color=YELLOW, label="2^t")
top = mark_point(stage, ax, 6, 64, label="64")
stage.caption("Each hour adds more than all before")

beats.intent: A straight line 10t on the same axes falling far below the doubling curve
beats.narration: Compare a steady ten per hour: after six hours it is only at sixty, and it will never catch up again.
beats.code:
lin = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda t: 10 * t, color=GREEN, label="10t")
stage.caption("Doubling soon beats any steady rate")

request: why does growth slow down when resources run out?

beats.intent: Axes with an S-shaped logistic curve rising from 5 towards 100
beats.narration: A population in a pond grows fast at first, then levels off.
beats.code:
stage.title("Growth with a limit")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 12), y_range=(0, 120), labels=("time", "fish"))
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda t: 100 / (1 + 19 * np.exp(-0.7 * t)), color=BLUE)
stage.caption("Fast at first, then it levels off")

beats.intent: A dashed horizontal line at 100 labelled carrying capacity
beats.narration: The pond can only feed about a hundred fish. That ceiling is the carrying capacity.
beats.code:
cap = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(0, 100), ax.c2p(12, 100), color=RED, dashed=True)
stage.label(cap, "carrying capacity 100", direction=UP, color=RED)

beats.intent: A tangent sliding along the curve, steepest in the middle, flat at the ends
beats.narration: The growth rate is the slope: small at the start, largest halfway up, and nearly zero near the ceiling.
beats.code:
slide_tangent(stage, ax, lambda t: 100 / (1 + 19 * np.exp(-0.7 * t)), 1, 11)
stage.caption("Fastest growth at half the limit")

request: how do you read speed off a table of distances?

beats.intent: Axes of seconds against metres with five measured points in a straight row
beats.narration: A runner's distance is measured every two seconds: zero, ten, twenty, thirty, forty metres.
beats.code:
stage.title("Speed from a table")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 10), y_range=(0, 50), labels=("s", "m"))
pts = plot_points(stage, ax, [(0, 0), (2, 10), (4, 20), (6, 30), (8, 40)])
stage.caption("Distance every two seconds")

beats.intent: A line through the points and a right triangle showing 10 metres up for 2 seconds across
beats.narration: Join them up. Each step across of two seconds goes up ten metres.
beats.code:
line = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda t: 5 * t, color=YELLOW)
run = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(2, 10), ax.c2p(4, 10), color=GREEN)
rise = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(4, 10), ax.c2p(4, 20), color=RED)
stage.label(run, "2 s", direction=DOWN, color=GREEN)
stage.label(rise, "10 m", direction=RIGHT, color=RED)

beats.intent: The equation speed = 10 m / 2 s = 5 m/s beside the graph
beats.narration: Rise over run is the speed: ten metres per two seconds, five metres per second.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\text{speed} = \frac{10\,\text{m}}{2\,\text{s}}", r"= 5\ \text{m/s}")

request: how high does a ball go when you throw it straight up?

beats.intent: Axes of time against height with the ball's measured heights as dots
beats.narration: We measure the ball's height every half second after throwing it up at twenty metres per second.
beats.code:
stage.title("A ball thrown upward")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 4), y_range=(0, 25), labels=("s", "m"))
data = [(t, 20 * t - 5 * t * t) for t in (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4)]
pts = plot_points(stage, ax, data)
stage.caption("Height every half second")

beats.intent: The parabola h = 20t - 5t^2 drawn through the dots
beats.narration: The dots lie on a parabola: height equals twenty t minus five t squared.
beats.code: h = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda t: 20 * t - 5 * t * t, color=YELLOW, label="h = 20t - 5t^2")

beats.intent: The top of the parabola marked at t = 2, height 20, with a flat tangent
beats.narration: The ball stops rising at two seconds, twenty metres up, where the curve is flat.
beats.code:
top = mark_point(stage, ax, 2, 20, color=RED, label="20 m at 2 s")
flat = draw_line(stage, ax.c2p(1.2, 20), ax.c2p(2.8, 20), color=RED, dashed=True)
stage.caption("Highest point: slope zero")

request: how many handshakes happen when six people meet?

beats.intent: Six dots in a ring, one per person
beats.narration: Six people stand in a circle.
beats.code:
stage.title("Six people, every pair shakes hands")
names = "ABCDEF"
nodes = {n: (0.9 * np.cos(TAU * k / 6), 0.9 * np.sin(TAU * k / 6)) for k, n in enumerate(names)}
dots, lines = draw_network(stage, nodes, [])

beats.intent: Person A joined by lines to the five others
beats.narration: The first person shakes hands with the other five.
beats.code:
dots2, first = draw_network(stage, nodes, [("A", b) for b in "BCDEF"])
stage.caption("A shakes 5 hands")

beats.intent: All 15 lines between the six dots drawn
beats.narration: The next shakes four new hands, then three, two, one. Five plus four plus three plus two plus one is fifteen.
beats.code:
dots3, all_lines = draw_network(stage, nodes, [(a, b) for i, a in enumerate(names) for b in names[i + 1:]])
stage.equation(r"5+4+3+2+1 = 15", r"\frac{6 \times 5}{2} = 15")

beats.narration: Count by rows: four, eight, twelve.

request: smoothing noisy measurements with a moving average

beats.intent: Axes with 20 jittery temperature readings as dots
beats.narration: Twenty temperature readings, bouncing up and down around a slow trend.
beats.code:
stage.title("Noisy readings")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 20), y_range=(0, 30), labels=("day", "°C"))
noise = [2.1, -1.8, 1.2, -2.4, 0.6, 2.7, -1.1, -2.0, 1.9, 0.3, -1.6, 2.2, -0.8, 1.4, -2.3, 0.9, 1.7, -1.3, 0.4, -0.6]
raw = [(d, 10 + 0.6 * d + noise[d]) for d in range(20)]
pts = plot_points(stage, ax, raw)

beats.intent: A window of three neighbouring dots highlighted and their average marked
beats.narration: Take three neighbouring days and average them. The ups and downs partly cancel.
beats.code:
highlight(stage, VGroup(*pts[4:7]))
avg = sum(y for _, y in raw[4:7]) / 3
m = mark_point(stage, ax, 5, avg, color=RED, label="average")

beats.intent: A smooth red curve of the 3-day averages drawn through the cloud
beats.narration: Slide that window along every day and join the averages: the trend appears.
beats.code:
sm = [(d, sum(y for _, y in raw[d - 1:d + 2]) / 3) for d in range(1, 19)]
curve = VMobject(color=RED).set_points_smoothly([ax.c2p(x, y) for x, y in sm])
stage.play(Create(curve), run_time=2)
stage.caption("The moving average shows the trend")

request: how does a stretched spring obey Hooke's law?

beats.intent: Axes of force against stretch with five measured points
beats.narration: Hang weights on a spring and measure how far it stretches: the points fall on a line.
beats.code:
stage.title("Hooke's law")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 10), y_range=(0, 50), labels=("cm", "N"))
pts = plot_points(stage, ax, [(2, 10), (4, 20), (6, 30), (8, 40)])

beats.intent: The line F = 5x through the origin and every point
beats.narration: The force is five newtons for every centimetre: F equals five x.
beats.code:
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: 5 * x, color=YELLOW, label="F = 5x")
stage.caption("Twice the stretch, twice the force")

beats.intent: The triangle under the line to x = 8 shaded, its area the stored energy
beats.narration: The area under the line is the energy stored in the spring: a triangle, half of eight times forty.
beats.code:
shade_area(stage, ax, g, 0, 8)
stage.equation(r"E = \tfrac12 \cdot 8 \cdot 40 = 160 \ \text{N·cm}")

request: mean of a data set as a balance point

beats.intent: Five dots on a number line from 0 to 10 at 1, 3, 4, 7 and 10
beats.narration: Five values sit on a number line like weights on a plank.
beats.code:
stage.title("The balance point")
nl = draw_number_line(stage, x_range=(0, 10))
ws = [mark_point(stage, nl, v) for v in (1, 3, 4, 7, 10)]

beats.intent: A triangle under the line at 5, the mean, with distances to each dot shown
beats.narration: Put the pivot at the mean, five. The distances to the left add to seven, and to the right also seven.
beats.code:
piv = Triangle(color=RED, fill_opacity=0.8).scale(0.2).next_to(nl.n2p(5), DOWN, buff=0.05)
stage.play(FadeIn(piv))
left = draw_line(stage, nl.n2p(1) + UP * 0.5, nl.n2p(5) + UP * 0.5, color=BLUE)
right = draw_line(stage, nl.n2p(5) + UP * 0.8, nl.n2p(10) + UP * 0.8, color=GREEN)
stage.equation(r"(5-1)+(5-3)+(5-4) = 7", r"(7-5)+(10-5) = 7")

beats.intent: The equation mean = (1+3+4+7+10)/5 = 5 beside the balanced line
beats.narration: The mean is the point where the data balance.
beats.code:
stage.equation(r"\bar{x} = \frac{1+3+4+7+10}{5} = 5")
stage.caption("The mean balances the data")
